system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only references preserve their role-specific recipient and do not play the original recording; voice, new-score style, cut/action timing and new sound texture are distinct relationships, never general permission to condition any new sound. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The typed claims preserve their explicit origins. A user-origin claim records caller authorization or a requested outcome; it is not itself evidence that the final narrative executes that outcome or copies an original signal. User claims are deliberately absent from executable fragment addresses. Compare the actual final narrative, source bindings and typed performance events to that authorization. Observed and creative claims remain auditable executable assertions.
The request has multiple identity-source candidates. Check subject_projections and the caller's complete request: one identifiable target may combine separately selected properties from several sources. Every requested source/property contribution must be present in that target's actual typed attributes and source attribution details, consistent with subject_projections and the quoted caller requirements. A descriptor or summary claiming a contribution does not replace a missing typed attribute or the wrong source/property selection. The subject definition fragments expose the complete ledger for exact finding quotes. Reject subject_projection_mismatch when a requested contribution is missing or assigned to the wrong source, or when the final actual narrative clearly duplicates that same requested target as separate actors, combines distinct requested actors contrary to the request, changes the selected target category (for example a car into an unspecified object), or imports source properties that its accepted projection excluded, including properties sneaked into its target descriptor. A new unrelated permitted actor is not automatically a duplicate. Cite the exact contradictory final fragment. Source resemblance alone is not identity authorization.
projection_source_bindings is the host-owned PRE-projection subject-ID/conditioning-label/asset-ID graph. Source IDs in subject_projections refer to that graph, whereas target_subjects contains only the final surviving identities after selected sources are merged. A consumed source ID need not survive as a separate target; do not mistake that absence for lost provenance or use final target positions to reassign sources. Source asset IDs and typed edges settle the selected source, not ordinal words inside an attribute's original caller wording. Audit the actual source/property edges using these bindings and the final attribution details.

claims.text: Define it once as a single subject that draws its body from the first picture and its wheels from the second.
The car is presented in a dim industrial bay with dark asphalt, cool overhead light and distant amber warmth.
The car idles, rolls forward and accelerates away, leaving the frame.
Newly generated engine and tyre sounds accompany the movement.
A restrained low electronic score plays quietly beneath the vehicle sounds.

fragments.music: A restrained low electronic pulse and faint metallic shimmer at a slow tempo, mixed beneath the engine and tyre sounds.
fragments.shot:shot-1:description: The scene opens in a low, wide industrial bay with a smooth dark asphalt floor and distant cool overhead strips. <Subject:subject-2> sits settled on the asphalt, the carbon fibre body catching long bands of pale light while the selected wheels remain planted and clearly readable at the corners. A faint amber warmth from far lamps touches the roofline, and the glossy floor holds a soft reflection beneath the car. The engine is already running at a low, even idle, and the whole vehicle reads as one composite machine rather than two separate references. Small vibrations travel through the bodywork, but the wheels stay still and the stance remains composed.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: The engine settles into a low idle while the <Subject:subject-2> remains still on the asphalt.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:1: A low idling engine note and a faint tyre contact hum fill the bay.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: A brief vibration passes through the bodywork and the reflection on the floor trembles.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: The view moves closer to the lower body of <Subject:subject-2>, where the selected wheels dominate the frame. The tyres flex against the asphalt, then begin to rotate, their tread and rims turning with the forward motion. The car eases ahead in a steady roll, the carbon fibre flanks drawing bright streaks from the overhead lights as the wheels gather speed. Dust and fine grit lift lightly from the floor, and the reflection under the car stretches and breaks. The body stays low and controlled while the rotation of the wheels becomes the clearest sign that the vehicle is now moving.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: The tyres flex, then begin to rotate as the <Subject:subject-2> rolls forward.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: Tyres roll over asphalt with a soft, gritty hum.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: The car eases ahead in a steady roll, the carbon fibre flanks catching bright streaks.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: The engine note rises as the wheels gather speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:4: The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-3:description: The car drives out across the open floor, <Subject:subject-2> accelerating smoothly as the carbon fibre body flashes with passing light. The wheels spin faster, throwing a thin scatter of grit and a short pulse of air across the asphalt. The vehicle rolls toward the far edge, its reflection slipping away behind it, while the engine note climbs and the cool bay light rakes along the roof and rear haunches. The car clears the far edge of the frame, leaving the dark floor, the last amber rim light and a fading trail of tyre noise behind.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:0: The <Subject:subject-2> accelerates smoothly across the open floor, light sliding over the carbon fibre body.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:1: The engine note climbs while a short rush of air crosses the bodywork.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:2: The wheels spin faster and a thin scatter of grit lifts from the asphalt.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:3: Tyre noise fades toward the far edge of the bay.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:4: The camera arcs around the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.soundscape: A low, newly generated engine idle that rises into a measured rev, with soft tyre contact hum over asphalt and a light rush of air across the bodywork.
